topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: The Hook: Which Path is Fastest?
lecture_lines: Can a sliding bead move faster on a curve?
Intuition suggests the straight line is fastest.
Yet, a deep curve wins the race.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Conservation of Energy
lecture_lines: Gravity converts potential energy to kinetic energy.
Speed increases as the bead descends.
Time is the integral of distance over speed.
animations: Display potential energy formula U=mgh at #FFFFFF.
Display kinetic energy formula K=1/2mv^2 at #FFFFFF.
Show conversion of energy as [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] descends at #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Calculus of Variations
lecture_lines: We seek a path minimizing total travel time.
This is a problem for calculus of variations.
The functional depends on the path shape.
Small changes in path alter total time.
We look for the stationary point of time.
animations: Highlight the functional to be minimized at #00FFFF.
Show infinitesimal change in path shape using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/path.svg] at #FF00FF.
Display differential variation of the path at #FF00FF.
Summarize the optimization condition clearly using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/time.svg] at #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
lecture_lines: The optimal path is called a cycloid.
It is traced by a point on rolling wheels.
This curve perfectly balances distance and speed.
Steeper starts build velocity for the end.
The cycloid is the true fastest path.

sections.title: Real-World Synthesis
lecture_lines: Cycloids appear often in nature and physics.
Pendulums use this property to keep time.
Birds of prey dive using cycloid paths.
